jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Algeria has no AI-specific law; AI is governed through strategy documents, sector guidance and the general personal-data law. The binding layer is Law 18-07 of 2018 on personal data, overseen by the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (ANPDP) and substantially amended by Law 25-11 of July 2025, which adds profiling and biometric definitions, data protection officers, processing registers and, for criminal-justice processing, limits on automated decisions and impact assessments. The High Commission for Digitalization's National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025–2030 (validated August 2024) mentions AI only as an enabling technology for digital governance. A dedicated National AI Strategy, built on data, digital infrastructure and skills, was examined by the Government on 25 May 2026 and is being implemented through sector committees chaired by the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MESRS), but its text has not been published. In higher education, the 2023 university ethics charter and a note on digital ethics set out AI-ethics expectations.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MESRS)
High Commission for Digitalization (Haut-Commissariat à la Numérisation), Presidency of the Republic

narrative.review_notes: A deep review completed on 7 October 2026 searched every issue of the Official Journal from 2019 to October 2026 for artificial intelligence; texts that only set up AI schools or research units were not recorded as governance documents, and titles follow the French edition while the authentic Arabic text is linked on each document. The websites of the data protection authority, the Prime Minister's office, the Bank of Algeria, the Presidency, the cybersecurity agency and the digital ministry were unavailable, and the national AI strategy, examined by the Government in May 2026, is pending until its text is published.

instruments.current_status: In force; published in Journal officiel No. 34 of 10 June 2018 (Arabic text authentic; French edition is the official translation). Art. 75 gives existing processors one year from the installation of the National Authority (ANPDP) to comply; no single commencement date is stated. Amended and completed by Law No. 25-11 of 24 July 2025, which repealed Arts. 10 and 11.
instruments.summary: Algeria's general personal-data law: it sets lawful-processing principles, prior declaration or authorisation of processing with the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (ANPDP), data-subject rights, cross-border transfer limits and criminal penalties. As adopted, Art. 11 barred decisions with legal effects from being based solely on automated processing that profiles a person; Law 25-11 of 2025 repealed Arts. 10 and 11 and moved a similar rule into a new title on criminal-justice processing. The law binds public and private controllers, so it governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.

instruments.publisher_name: President of the Republic (law adopted by Parliament)
instruments.current_status: Published in Journal officiel No. 48 of 24 July 2025 (Arabic text authentic; French edition is the official translation). The law states no separate commencement date; some provisions (ANPDP regional poles) require implementing regulations.
instruments.summary: Amends Law 18-07: adds definitions of biometric data, profiling and pseudonymisation; requires controllers and competent authorities to appoint a data protection officer and to keep a register of processing activities and an automated log of processing operations; and creates ANPDP regional audit poles. A new Title V bis on processing for crime prevention, investigation, prosecution and sentencing bans judicial or other legal-effect decisions based solely on automated profiling, requires a prior impact assessment where new technologies create high risk, and imposes 5-day breach notification to the ANPDP; it also repeals Arts. 10 and 11 of Law 18-07. These rules matter for profiling and biometric systems, including AI-based ones.
metadata_gaps: Commencement date not stated in the law

instruments.summary: Algeria's national digital transformation strategy for 2025–2030, built on five axes (ICT infrastructure, human capital and training, digital governance, digital economy, digital society) and 25 strategic objectives, with a planned overarching digital law and alignment with the national information-systems security framework. AI is not a separate pillar: the digital-governance axis names AI and the Internet of Things as emerging technologies to be introduced for modernising public administration. It guides ministries and public bodies but is not binding.

instruments.current_status: August 2023 edition prepared by the National Council for Ethics and Deontology of the University Profession at the Minister's request; it updates the 2010 charter. MESRS invites members of the university community to sign it. Related: the National Council for Ethics and Deontology's 'Note sur l'éthique numérique' of 2 August 2023 (https://services.mesrs.dz/cned/download/Note_sur_ethique_numerique_2_Aout_2023.pdf) develops the charter's digital-ethics and AI points; it is not recorded as a separate instrument.
instruments.summary: The charter of ethics and professional conduct for the whole public and private university community. Its new section 1.7 on digital ethics requires institutions to secure data, protect privacy, counter manipulation and discrimination from biased algorithms and datasets, and contribute to frameworks for the ethical governance of AI in higher education and research. It applies to staff and students as a sector code, not as legislation.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Every issue of the Official Journal from 2019 to 2026, regulators and the standards body and, in a later search on 2026-10-13, each national ministry were searched for official AI material. None was found for binding AI law, founding texts of AI governance bodies, risk and assurance, public-sector rules, procurement, AI security guidance, transparency, AI standards, sandboxes, government AI indices, generative-AI guidance, published drafts or consultations, national AI treaties or superseded instruments; regional instruments apply through the regional pages. coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 7 October 2026. Every issue of the Official Journal from 2019 to October 2026 was searched for artificial intelligence; texts that only set up AI schools or research units were not recorded as governance instruments. Titles follow the French edition of the Official Journal; the Arabic text is authentic and is linked on each record. The websites of the data protection authority, the Prime Minister's office, the Bank of Algeria, the Presidency, the cybersecurity agency and the digital ministry could not be read. The national AI strategy, examined by the Government in May 2026, is pending until its text is published.

Coverage note (original): Searched and found no official AI-specific material for: binding AI law, AI governance body founding texts (no decree for the AI scientific council or national AI council in the Journal officiel 2019–2026), risk/assurance, public-sector AI rules, AI procurement, AI security guidance (ASSI), transparency, AI standards (IANOR catalogue to 31 Dec 2025 has no ISO/IEC 42001 or other AI standard), sandboxes, government AI indices, generative-AI guidance, published drafts or consultations, national treaties on AI, and superseded AI instruments. Regional instruments (AU Continental AI Strategy; UNESCO Recommendation) apply through data/regional. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-07. The French edition of every Journal officiel issue from 2019 to issue 69 of 2026 (about 690 PDFs from joradp.dz) was downloaded and searched for 'intelligence artificielle'. The hits are founding and organisation texts for the Ecole nationale supérieure en intelligence artificielle (from 2021), research-unit orders, a 2025 MESRS order creating an AI thematic research network (DZAIR) under the ATRST, and an occupational-safety decree defining automated work. These are education or research infrastructure, not AI governance, and are not recorded. Presidential Decree 23-314 of 6 September 2023 creating the High Commission for Digitalization does not mention AI and is not recorded. Official titles are given from the French edition of the Journal officiel; the Arabic text is authentic, and the Arabic PDF links are kept in official_webpage_url. Sites that blocked or failed automated reading: anpdp.dz (HTTP 500), premier-ministre.gov.dz and bank-of-algeria.dz (TLS certificate chain not verifiable via the proxy), el-mouradia.dz, assi.dz, mpttn.gov.dz and numerisation.gov.dz (connection reset or 502), univ-jijel.dz (connection reset). No news agency or aggregator is used as a source. The national AI strategy, adopted at the African Start-up Conference (December 2024) and examined by the Government on 25 May 2026, is held as a lead until an official text is published. The 2 August 2023 note on digital ethics is not recorded separately; its URL is cited in the Charter of University Deontology and Ethics record. Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 0 record(s) added. Ethics charter (Aug 2023) already recorded and the CNED 'Note sur l'éthique numérique' already referenced in it; nothing new recorded; new lead: CSIA founding instrument; Ministry of National Education: site searched (ar); only news items (robotics/AI competition, UNESCO AI-ethics course); nothing found; Ministry of Health: site unreachable (curl connection reset; WebFetch 503); search found only a 2023 digital-health strategy project reported in news, not AI-specific and no official text;
